subject: Accounting
title: Revenue Accounts
description: A fast breakdown of Revenue Accounts for builders.

hook.text: A coffee shop sells 200 lattes on Monday. That $1,000 flows into one place: revenue.

buildup.text: Revenue accounts track all income earned from normal business operations.

discovery.text: Sales revenue, service revenue, interest income—each gets its own line in the records.

twist.text: Revenue isn't profit. A store can have millions in revenue and still lose money.

climax.text: Tracking revenue by category helps businesses spot which products actually perform.

punchline.text: Revenue is the top line. Profit is what survives.

details.summary: Revenue accounts record income earned from a company's primary business activities—product sales, service fees, subscription income, and other operating activities. This topic covers revenue recognition principles and how revenue accounts function.
details.whyItMatters: Revenue is the top line that drives everything below it on the income statement. Misreporting revenue—intentionally or accidentally—is the most common form of financial statement fraud.
takeaways: Revenue is recognized when earned — when goods are delivered or services performed — not when cash is received
The five-step revenue recognition model under ASC 606 standardizes when and how revenue is recorded
Revenue accounts are temporary accounts that reset to zero at the end of each accounting period

faq.question: When is revenue recognized in accounting?
faq.answer: Under ASC 606, revenue is recognized when performance obligations are satisfied—when the promised goods or services are transferred to the customer. The five steps are: identify the contract, identify obligations, determine price, allocate price, and recognize upon satisfaction.

faq.question: What is the difference between revenue and cash receipts?
faq.answer: Revenue is earned when goods or services are delivered; cash receipts happen when money is received. A company can earn revenue in December (delivering goods) but not receive cash until January. These are recorded as revenue and accounts receivable, respectively.
